entries.boundary: Depends on the declared threshold, which is author-set. GD_min is the threshold-free companion.
entries.claim: Gate divergence against the enterprise's predeclared heat-map rule at the declared threshold T_H = 15.

entries.interpretation: Register rows on which the approved gate assignment differs from the scalar heat-map comparator at the declared threshold. Both sums run over all 16 rows, non-runtime dispositions included.

entries.boundary: Case A's GD_min sums over all 16 rows, three of which carry documented fixture ratings; the published sweep gives the range [2, 5].
entries.claim: Minimum gate divergence over all thresholds. GD_min > 0 instantiates the Proposition 1 premise.
entries.inputs: cases/case_a/inputs/, cases/case_a/judgment/, cases/case_a/dispositions/, cases/case_a/acs/, catalog/, invariants/
entries.interpretation: Case A's GD_min > 0 means no monotone threshold on the scalar score reproduces the approved assignment. Case B's GD_min = 0 means that register does admit one -- reported rather than suppressed.

entries.boundary: Depends on the declared threshold, which is author-set. GD_min is the threshold-free companion.

entries.boundary: Discloses that the reported GD_min is contingent on three documented fixtures. Neither proposition premise depends on them.

entries.interpretation: Sweep over every (L, I) in {1..5}^2 for R-14, R-15 and R-16 -- 15625 combinations. The published ratings are {"R-14": 12, "R-15": 6, "R-16": 8}.

entries.boundary: TD is a property of the CANONICAL PAYLOAD HASH; the signature envelope need not be byte-identical. Measured on one implementation -- specification-level determinism, which would need a second independent implementation, is NOT established.
entries.claim: Translation determinism is 1.000: every run reproduced the committed reference canonical payload hash.
entries.interpretation: Semantically equivalent inputs compile to the same canonical payload hash under permutation, locale, time-zone and clean-process variation.

entries.boundary: A run count, not an environment count.
entries.claim: 62 compilation runs in total.
entries.interpretation: 31 runs per case across the two cases.

entries.boundary: A stratified design fixed before execution, not a random sample.
entries.claim: 31 runs per case, following the frozen stratified matrix.
entries.interpretation: Strata: {"key_shuffle": 5, "locale": 3, "repeat": 10, "row_shuffle": 10, "timezone": 3}.

entries.boundary: Covers the perturbation classes enumerated in the freeze, not all possible input perturbations.
entries.claim: 10 clean repeats, 10 row shuffles, 5 object-key shuffles, 3 locales and 3 time zones.
entries.interpretation: The frozen 10+10+5+3+3 design, 31 per case.

entries.boundary: Sampling under a declared model, not an empirical frequency.
entries.claim: The Monte Carlo analysis is executed at K = 250,000 draws.
entries.interpretation: Frozen draw count; RNG seed 20260201.

entries.boundary: Reproducibility of the simulation, not of reality.
entries.claim: The Monte Carlo seed is frozen in the preregistration.
entries.interpretation: Makes the draw sequence reproducible bit for bit.

entries.boundary: AUTHOR-SPECIFIED, prospectively frozen +/-1 ordinal sensitivity model. NOT panel-adjudicated -- no adjudication panel has been convened -- and NOT an estimate of real rating uncertainty.
entries.claim: Rating perturbation moves heat-map gate membership with probability up to 0.321.
entries.interpretation: Maximum per-risk heat-map flip probability, on row R-06 (approved score 15).

entries.boundary: Quantifies simulation noise only, never model uncertainty.
entries.claim: Monte Carlo standard error on the headline flip probability.
entries.interpretation: Sampling error at K = 250,000. The paper rounds it to 0.001.

entries.boundary: Structural, given the declared C* profile. Proposition 3 carries the claim; the simulation corroborates it rather than proving it.
entries.claim: Consequence-class membership does not move at all under the same perturbation.
entries.interpretation: C* membership is not a function of the perturbed ratings. This corroborates Proposition 3.

entries.boundary: 1,000 probe draws, not all 250,000.
entries.claim: The C* zero is verified by re-running the approved classifier on 1,000 perturbed draws, not assumed.
entries.interpretation: Direct verification rather than an argument from construction.
entries.metric: C* membership changes over probe draws

entries.boundary: A second declared model, still author-specified.
entries.claim: Under a variant that renormalizes out-of-scale mass instead of reassigning it, the maximum flip probability is 0.352.
entries.interpretation: Shows the headline figure is not knife-edge on the out-of-scale mass rule.

entries.boundary: AUTHOR-SPECIFIED, prospectively frozen +/-1 ordinal sensitivity model. NOT panel-adjudicated -- no adjudication panel has been convened -- and NOT an estimate of real rating uncertainty.
entries.claim: Over the draws, GD at the declared threshold has mean 5.447 against an approved value of 3.
entries.interpretation: Distributional summary under the frozen model.

entries.boundary: AUTHOR-SPECIFIED, prospectively frozen +/-1 ordinal sensitivity model. NOT panel-adjudicated -- no adjudication panel has been convened -- and NOT an estimate of real rating uncertainty.
entries.claim: GD_min has mean 3.226 over the draws.
entries.interpretation: Distributional summary under the frozen model.

entries.boundary: AUTHOR-SPECIFIED, prospectively frozen +/-1 ordinal sensitivity model. NOT panel-adjudicated -- no adjudication panel has been convened -- and NOT an estimate of real rating uncertainty.
entries.claim: The expected number of heat-map gate changes per register is 3.64.
entries.interpretation: Distributional summary under the frozen model.

entries.boundary: A finite list of known failure modes. Not a proof of robustness.
entries.claim: The adversarial corpus is 62 cases, all passing.
entries.interpretation: A case counts as passing only if it is rejected with the error code its requirement predicts; code_mismatch = 0, so rejection for an unrelated reason would not count.

entries.boundary: Structural, not semantic.
entries.claim: 26 structural checks, all passing.
entries.interpretation: Structural invariants of the compiled bundle.

entries.boundary: Three specific seeded conditions.
entries.claim: Three seeded validation rows behave as specified.
entries.interpretation: Deliberately seeded WC-01 and RC-05 rows, exercised rather than described.

entries.boundary: Decision-level injections against the compiled Case B predicate set. These establish that the compiled bundle refuses to permit under each hazard class the published enforcement artifact enumerates. They are NOT a run over the 284,807-event corpus, establish NO detection performance, and reproduce no figure from [15].
entries.claim: The thirteen Case B injection scenarios all resolve to SAFE_STATE against a clean PERMIT control.
entries.interpretation: The eight adversarial attack families and five ASB scenario families enumerated by the consuming enforcement artifact.

entries.boundary: Tests, not proofs.
entries.claim: 280 tests pass across the four suites.
entries.interpretation: Unit, property-based, adversarial and integration suites; 0 failures, 0 errors.

entries.boundary: Property-based tests sample; they do not verify, except where the space is exhausted.
entries.claim: 16 properties over 1,427 generated examples.
entries.interpretation: Hypothesis, max_examples = 100 per property. Two properties report fewer because their finite input spaces are EXHAUSTED, which is stronger evidence than 100 random draws.

entries.boundary: Empty result sets on the clean fixtures demonstrate linkage and temporal-integrity completeness UNDER THE DECLARED DATA MODEL. They do not establish legal compliance, semantic correctness, or control effectiveness. The negative controls establish that each query can in fact detect the violation it exists to detect.
entries.claim: All six traceability audit queries return empty on the clean fixtures, for both cases.
entries.interpretation: Linkage and temporal-integrity completeness under the declared data model. Queries: Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6.

entries.boundary: Establishes query sensitivity on seeded faults, not exhaustiveness over all possible faults.
entries.claim: Every negative control fires.
entries.interpretation: Each query can in fact detect the violation it exists to detect, so an empty clean result is informative rather than vacuous.

entries.boundary: Establishes prospective public commitment for TIER-0 only. The Tier-1 held-out register is not covered and is not yet authored.
entries.claim: The public preregistration commitment is discharged: the freeze tag was pushed to the remote BEFORE the reportable campaign executed.
entries.interpretation: Tag preregister-tier0-v2.2 at commit c44f25d6fdb6; the remote tag dereferences to the same commit.

entries.boundary: Frozen scope, NOT repository scope. MANIFEST.sha256 inventories the wider repository and serves a different purpose.
entries.claim: The freeze manifest covers 133 files.
entries.interpretation: The scope of the frozen scientific experiment.

entries.boundary: NOT platform independence. A finite matrix of environments is not the set of all environments; no other operating system and no other Python implementation was exercised.
entries.claim: TD = 1.000 with identical reference canonical payload hashes on eight independently provisioned environments spanning three operating systems, two machine architectures and six CPython patch versions.
entries.expected: TD = 1.0 and matching reference hashes on every leg
entries.experiment: cross-platform determinism (GitHub Actions matrix, pinned container, local host)
entries.interpretation: Determinism reproduces across the tested supported environments; 496 compilations in total.
entries.reported: 8 environments, all TD = 1.000, all reference hashes identical
